title: "Group Project"

  html:
    toc: true
---

> Each group picks three questions about one of two new datasets, works on them
> in pairs over two mornings, and on Friday presents to a group that worked on
> the other dataset. We do not give you an answer to check against.

## Groups and pairs

There are ten groups of six people. Five groups (A1 to A5) take Study A and five
(B1 to B5) take Study B. You meet your group on Wednesday morning.

Inside your group you work in three pairs, and each pair takes one
sub-question. Both partners work on the same sub-question separately, each in
their own Codespace with their own Pi, and you do not compare notes until the
first check-in. Pi will usually take a different route for each of you, and
working out why is most of the job.

On Friday each Study A group pairs with the Study B group of the same number and
sits with them. A1 presents to B1, then B1 presents to A1; A2 and B2 do the same
nearby, and so on. Your audience has spent two mornings on a different dataset,
so explain your study before your result.

## Wednesday

By Wednesday morning you have done count-table anatomy and ordination.
Differential testing is on Wednesday afternoon.

| time | who | what |
|---|---|---|
| 9:00 | group | Meet. |
| 9:10 | everyone | Ask Pi questions about your dataset. Do not ask for code yet. What is in each file, how many people are in each arm, what does a column mean, what is Amsel? |
| 9:30 | group | Pick three sub-questions from the menu below and form pairs. In each pair, decide who takes which model. |
| 9:40 | each person | Write the [QC report](#the-qc-report). |
| 10:00 | | Tea |
| 10:15 | each person | Finish the QC report, then start on your sub-question. |
| **10:45** | **pair** | [Check-in W1](#check-ins) |
| 11:00 | each person | Ask Pi for whatever your QC report missed, then carry on with your sub-question. |
| **11:45** | **group** | [Check-in W2](#check-ins) |
| 12:05 | each person | Rerun with the group's QC decision and carry on. Before lunch, write a few lines at the top of your `.qmd` saying where you got to. |
| 12:30 | | Lunch |

: {tbl-colwidths="[12,14,74]"}

## Thursday

By Thursday morning you have done differential testing too. Sets and enrichment
is on Thursday afternoon, after the group work.

| time | who | what |
|---|---|---|
| 9:00 | pair | Read yesterday's notes and swap models. |
| 9:05 | each person | Ask your new model to review your `.qmd` from yesterday: "Read this document and critique the choices made. What would you do differently?" Decide what to change. |
| 10:00 | | Tea |
| 10:15 | each person | Carry on and render your final figures. |
| **10:45** | **pair** | [Check-in T1](#check-ins) |
| 11:00 | each person | Put your figures in the deck. |
| **11:45** | **group** | [Check-in T2](#check-ins) |
| 12:05 | group | Finish the slides. |
| 12:30 | | Lunch |

: {tbl-colwidths="[12,14,74]"}

## Friday

| how long | what |
|---|---|
| 30 minutes | Run through your deck as a group. Each pair asks another pair one question about their slide. |
| 1 hour | Present to your paired group for 30 minutes, then listen to theirs for 30. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[20,80]"}

## Two models in each pair

On Wednesday one partner uses `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, the default, and the other
switches to `z-ai/glm-5.3` by typing `/model` in Pi. On Thursday you swap. The
stronger model costs roughly ten times as much for a morning's work, a couple
of dollars, which is still a small part of your budget.

If you are curious on Thursday, try `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` for a while.
Then look at what it cost on your [OpenRouter activity page](https://openrouter.ai/activity)
and decide for yourself whether it was worth it.

## Your group's deck

Each group gets a shared Google Slides deck on Wednesday morning. From the
start it has a slide for the group's QC decision and one open-questions slide
for each pair. Put anything you and your partner cannot explain yet on your
pair's open-questions slide, and note what you found out as you go, with a link
to whatever you read. On Thursday that slide becomes your "choice we made"
slide.

To get a figure into the deck, ask Pi to save it as a PNG in
`group_project/figures/`, then right-click the file in the Codespace file list
and choose **Download**.

## Study A: does a vaginal probiotic change the community?

A randomised trial. Participants received either a live *Lactobacillus crispatus*
product or a placebo, and were sampled before and after the course of treatment.

| | |
|---|---|
| participants | 176 |
| samples | 352, one before and one after per person |
| arms | 121 probiotic, 55 placebo |
| metadata | `arm`, `time_point` (`pre`, `post`), age, pH, Nugent score, Amsel criteria |

: {tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}

The arms are unbalanced, 121 against 55, so check your baseline before you
interpret anything about the follow-up.

### Study A sub-questions

We suggest one from each column, so that your three pairs cover the bacteria,
the host and the link between them.

| Microbiome | Host | Connecting the two |
|---|---|---|
| Did the community shift from pre to post, and differently by arm? *Tuesday's ordination is a good start.* | Did host gene expression change with treatment? *Wednesday afternoon's module covers this; on Wednesday morning, start by ordinating the genes.* | Did the probiotic only work in people whose community started a certain way? *Tuesday's community grouping is a good start.* |
| Which species changed in the probiotic arm, besides *L. crispatus*? *Wednesday afternoon's module covers this.* | Which biological processes do the gene changes point to? *Harder. Enrichment is taught on Thursday afternoon, so you will learn it from Pi and from reading.* | Do pH, Nugent score and cytokines move with the community change, or on their own? *Tuesday's anatomy module is a good start.* |

: {tbl-colwidths="[33,34,33]"}

## Study B: do hormonal contraceptives differ in their effect?

A cross-sectional comparison of three contraceptive methods, each person sampled
once.

| | |
|---|---|
| participants | 93, one sample each |
| arms | 39 injectable, 28 pill, 26 ring |
| metadata | `arm`, `bv` (Amsel), `nugent`, `ph`, `any_sti` |

: {tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}

The study is cross-sectional. Nobody was randomised to a method, and people who
choose different methods differ in other ways. With 93 samples in three groups,
ask which of your comparisons is actually powered.

### Study B sub-questions

We suggest one from each column.

| Microbiome | Host | Connecting the two |
|---|---|---|
| Do the three methods differ in community composition? *Tuesday's ordination is a good start.* | The ring is delivered locally and the other two are systemic. Does the ring differ from the other two in host gene expression? *Wednesday afternoon's module covers this; on Wednesday morning, start by ordinating the genes.* | Group people by community type, then test their genes. Does community type explain more than the method does? *Tuesday's community grouping is a good start.* |
| Is bacterial vaginosis more common in one arm? *Tuesday's anatomy module is a good start.* | Which biological processes do the ring-versus-systemic genes point to? *Harder. Enrichment is taught on Thursday afternoon, so you will learn it from Pi and from reading.* | Is bacterial vaginosis the explanation for whatever the method seems to do? *Start from your group's other two sub-questions.* |

: {tbl-colwidths="[33,34,33]"}

If your pair finishes early, write your own sub-question and tell the rest of
your group at the next check-in.

## The QC report

Everyone starts with the same prompt. Copy it into Pi as it is, with your
study's letter:

```
Make group_project/01-qc.qmd that checks the quality of the Study A data
before we analyse it. Render it.
```

The prompt is short on purpose. Your partner's model will decide differently
from yours what a quality check needs, and you will compare the two at 10:45.

## Check-ins

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## W1, Wednesday 10:45, with your partner

1. Open your two QC reports side by side. Does each one check

    - that sample IDs match across all the tables?
    - library sizes in both count tables, and which samples have very few reads?
    - missing metadata?
    - `rnaseq_batch` cross-tabulated against arm (and against time point in Study A)?
    - whether the arms differed at baseline (Study A)?

    For anything missing, ask your Pi to add it.
2. Compare the **Choices made** sections at the end of your two reports. For
   each difference, can either of you say why? If not, add it to your pair's
   open-questions slide.
3. Split the open questions between you.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## W2, Wednesday 11:45, the whole group

1. Each pair shows one figure and its open-questions slide, about three minutes
   per pair.
2. Answer each other's open questions where you can.
3. Agree one QC decision for the whole group: which samples you drop and how you
   filter features. Write it on the QC slide. All three pairs use it from now on.
4. What did your morning cost? Look at your OpenRouter activity page and compare
   the two models.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## T1, Thursday 10:45, with your partner

1. Which approach are you keeping, or are you keeping both to show the result
   does not depend on it? What is your reason, and what did you read that
   supports it?
2. Which one or two figures go in the talk?
3. Turn your open-questions slide into your "choice we made" slide.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## T2, Thursday 11:45, the whole group

1. Write the question for the whole talk in one sentence.
2. Put the slides in order.
3. State the answer as plainly as the data allow.
4. Write down what you do not believe about your own result.
5. Decide who is speaking.
:::

## Deliverables

A presentation that fits your 30-minute slot, containing:

1. the question you settled on, in one sentence
2. what you did, including what you filtered and why
3. two or three figures, each with a caption you read out
4. for each sub-question, a "choice we made" slide: the two routes you and your
   partner were given, which one you kept and why, and one source you opened and
   read yourself, even if Pi found it for you
5. the answer, stated as plainly as the data allow
6. what you do not believe about your own result

The last of these is required. When you are the audience, ask the other group
about theirs. Every analysis this week had something wrong with it, so look for
the problems in yours before you present.

## Advice from the modules

::: {.callout-tip}
## Things that bit people earlier in the week

- Check your sample table and your count matrix are in the same order before you
  run any test.
- Decide your filter before you look at the result, and write down why.
- On a species table, give DESeq2 `poscounts` size factors and check how many
  species they were built from.
- Define a grouping from one table and test the other, never the same table
  twice.
- Look at how lopsided a ranking is before you believe an enrichment.
- Your dataset has an `rnaseq_batch` column. Cross-tabulate it against your
  groups early, and find out whether you have a confound rather than a finding.
:::
